---
title: "Beads community analysis"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true
---

These are simulated communities. Run the chunks in order from the project root.
The aim is to distinguish species richness, evolutionary history, community
trait means, and trait dispersion, then compare sites with different habitats.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(picante)
d <- read_csv("data/samp.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
trait <- read_csv("data/dummy_trait.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
env <- read_csv("data/site_environment.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
tree <- read.tree("data/dummy_tree.newick")

samp <- tapply(d$abund, list(d$Site, d$Species), sum)
# Missing combinations must be verified as absences before replacing NA with 0.
stopifnot(!anyNA(samp), all(samp >= 0), all(rowSums(samp) > 0),
          !anyDuplicated(trait$sp), !anyDuplicated(env$site),
          setequal(colnames(samp), tree$tip.label),
          setequal(colnames(samp), trait$sp),
          setequal(rownames(samp), env$site))
```

## Richness and phylogenetic diversity

PD includes the path to the root (`include.root = TRUE`). MPD and MNTD below
use presence/absence, without abundance weighting. Branch lengths are arbitrary
units. High richness is intentional: some communities contain all 77 species
and therefore have the same presence/absence metrics.

```{r}
phylo_dm <- cophenetic(tree)
metrics <- tibble(
  site = rownames(samp),
  richness = vegan::specnumber(samp),
  shannon = vegan::diversity(samp),
  PD = pd(samp, tree, include.root = TRUE)$PD,
  MPD = mpd(samp, phylo_dm, abundance.weighted = FALSE),
  MNTD = mntd(samp, phylo_dm, abundance.weighted = FALSE)
) |>
  left_join(env, by = "site")
metrics
```

## Community-weighted means in original units

Each CWM is the sum of abundance × trait divided by total abundance. Align
species by name before matrix multiplication. This produces a site × trait
matrix. LMA remains in g m^-2^; wood density in g cm^-3^; seed mass in mg.

```{r}
aligned_trait <- trait[match(colnames(samp), trait$sp), ]
stopifnot(identical(aligned_trait$sp, colnames(samp)))
cwm <- (samp %*% as.matrix(aligned_trait[, -1])) / rowSums(samp)
cwm_sites <- as_tibble(cwm, rownames = "site") |>
  left_join(env, by = "site")
cwm_sites

ggplot(cwm_sites, aes(x = soil_moist, y = lma, color = topo, shape = type)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Moisture index", y = "CWM LMA (g m⁻²)") +
  theme_bw()
```

Compare CWM with richness: can the dominant strategy change while species
richness stays the same? Moisture is associated with topography, so this plot
alone cannot isolate their separate effects.

## Functional distances and a null expectation

Use log-transformed traits (except wood density), then standardize each trait.
This gives equal variance to each trait, although correlated traits still
represent overlapping information. These transformed values are used for
distances; the preceding CWM calculation uses original values.

```{r}
trait_for_distance <- trait |>
  mutate(across(c(lma, ll, a_mass, r_mass, n_mass, p_mass, sm), log))
trait_mat <- scale(as.matrix(trait_for_distance[, -1]))
rownames(trait_mat) <- trait$sp
trait_dm <- as.matrix(dist(trait_mat))
set.seed(123)
functional_mpd <- ses.mpd(samp, trait_dm, abundance.weighted = FALSE,
                          null.model = "taxa.labels", runs = 999)
# Full-pool communities have no label-shuffle variation; mask undefined SES.
full_pool <- rowSums(samp > 0) == nrow(trait_dm)
functional_mpd[full_pool, c("mpd.obs.z", "mpd.obs.p")] <- NA_real_
functional_mpd
```

The null model shuffles labels in the trait distance matrix, using the 77
species as the pool while preserving each site's richness. Negative SES means
smaller distances than the null mean; positive SES means larger distances.
The sign alone does not establish significance or identify an ecological
process. If every species in the pool is present, unweighted MPD is invariant
to label shuffles: the null SD is zero apart from numerical rounding, and
its SES is not interpretable.
